title: Legacy content, interoperability and the people a successor must serve
summary: The OpenSimulator hypergrid is the only existing "elsewhere" for SL communities: ~45k monthly actives and ~163k standard-region equivalents (Jan 2026) across hundreds of grids, regions priced $8-40/month, with OAR/IAR archives as the migration mechanism; but its largest free grid, OSgrid, wiped its database in March 2025 and was offline for weeks in May-June 2026 after an asset-filesystem failure. SL content export is governed by rights not formats: viewer export (Kokua/Firestorm) is creator-only, SL never adopted the OpenSim Export permission bit, the 2013 ToS Section 2.3 episode left creators distrustful, and Linden Lab's modernisation is slow (glTF mesh import mid-2024 to mid-2025, scene import decomposed in 2025, Project Zero browser streaming killed April 2026, mobile still beta, CCUG now discussing USD). Standards are converging on glTF (+VRM 1.0 for humanoids) for runtime and OpenUSD for scenes (AOUSD Core Spec 1.0 March 2026, ISO process for 1.1 July 2026, new characters/animation group), while proprietary avatar services (Ready Player Me, shut 31 Jan 2026 after Netflix acquisition) are dying and VRChat's Avatar Marketplace (May 2025, 600-credit floor, $100 payouts, undisclosed split) sets the economy comparator. The SL audience is older (sample means ~45 male / ~39 female), long-tenured, and organised around education (VWBPE, 2,200-3,500 attendees claimed), disability (Virtual Ability, 1,000+ members), live music (Cafe Musique 60+ shows/week) and roleplay; it is distinct from VRChat's ~120k weekend concurrents, Japan-heavy, younger VR crowd. Page fetching was blocked; all facts rest on search extracts, with gaps on current grid pricing, official SL/VRChat demographics and 2026 round-table content.
design_implications: Ship OAR and IAR import (terrain, objects, prim/sculpt/llmesh geometry, LSL script text, inventory) on day one; it is the only existing mass-migration path and the OpenSim diaspora already uses it after OSgrid's 2025 wipe and 2026 outage.
Adopt glTF 2.0 with VRM 1.0 extensions as the canonical runtime asset and OpenUSD as the scene/authoring interchange, matching where AOUSD, MSF and even Linden Lab's CCUG are heading.
Implement a creator-set Export permission bit from launch and honour it in every client; SL never shipped it and that absence is why SL content cannot legally follow residents.
Write the content licence in plain language with a defined 'affirmative action' clause for any platform re-use; the 2013 Section 2.3 episode is institutional memory among creators.
Provide a first-party, open-licensed Bento/BOM-class avatar body and a vendor opt-in programme, because SL avatar looks are no-mod third-party bodies that cannot be imported.
Prioritise stability, inventory integrity and reliable teleport over graphics features; those top resident complaints over twenty years and asset loss destroys trust (OSgrid).
Target desktop first and native mobile second; do not depend on a streamed browser viewer as the on-ramp (Project Zero was cancelled after 14 months).

Design for a 40-60-year-old, long-tenured audience: text-chat parity, accessibility (Virtual Ability, Radegast lineage), event tooling for live music and education, and land/group governance for roleplay sims.
Keep an economy with low minimum prices and creator-friendly, transparent payout terms; VRChat's 600-credit floor, $100 payout threshold and undisclosed split are the comparator to beat.
Price land competitively with hypergrid norms ($8-40/month per region) and consider Kitely-style idle-region suspension to make that sustainable.
open_questions: Current (2026) Kitely, DigiWorldz and OSgrid pricing and region counts, and whether OSgrid fully recovered after June 2026.
The actual July 2026 OpenSim active-user record figure (headline only was retrieved).
Whether Linden Lab will ship a glTF scene importer or an OpenUSD path, and its Land Impact rules for scenes.
Any post-2008 official Second Life demographic data (age, gender, tenure, country) and 2026 concurrency/daily-login figures.
VRChat's official age/gender split and the real Avatar Marketplace revenue share.
Whether major SL mesh-body vendors (Maitreya, Legacy, LeLutka etc.) would license bodies for an Export-enabled successor.
Firestorm's current export behaviour in SL and on OpenSim after the 2025-26 viewer merges.
Metaverse Standards Forum 2026 membership and the status of its avatar/wearables working groups.
Content of any 2026 Linden Lab Community Round Table and the 2026 roadmap statements.

claims.claim: Hypergrid Business's January 2026 tally counted public OpenSim at 162,771 standard-region equivalents, 44,867 monthly active users and 493,939 registered users (adjusted for an OSgrid user modelling all of North America, which inflated raw regions to ~988,206).

checks.note: HB Jan 15, 2026: 162,771 region equivalents, 44,867 actives, 493,939 registered with OSgrid adjustment; raw 988,206; 825,435 estimated North America experiment regions excluded.

claims.claim: OSgrid announced in February 2025 it would wipe its database on March 21, 2025, and in spring 2026 went offline for over three weeks after hitting asset-filesystem metadata size limits, with completion expected ~June 21-22, 2026.

checks.note: Feb 2025 wipe article (March 21, five weeks) exists; June 15, 2026 HB article: asset filesystem metadata size limits, third week down, tracker 40%->83%, expected June 21 (approximate). No source confirms reopening.

claims.claim: Linden Lab announced on April 21, 2026 that it was ending Project Zero, its AWS-streamed browser viewer, 14 months after launch, despite claiming in September 2025 a '10x' increase in people trying SL via Zero and the mobile app.

checks.note: End announced April 21, 2026 (post Apr 22), 14 months after launch, stayed in beta; May 2026 Web UG lists it closed, Lab calls it an experiment. The Sept 2025 '10x' figure was not in extracts (unverified sub-claim).

claims.claim: glTF mesh import in Second Life has been possible since mid-2024 with public viewer release mid-2025 (converted to llmesh); the full glTF scene importer was broken into smaller projects in April 2025; in July 2026 Geenz Linden solicited requests for an extensible glTF variant, with creators asking for hierarchies with proper origins and OpenUSD support.

checks.note: July 2, 2026 CCUG: Geenz Linden asked about an easier-to-extend glTF variant; requests included more material faces, glTF hierarchies with proper origins, OpenUSD support. mid-2024/mid-2025 import timeline and April 2025 decomposition not in extracts (unverified sub-claims).

claims.claim: Collada export in SL viewers (Kokua 2013, code from Singularity) honours permissions so only objects the user created can be exported; the OpenSim 'Export' permission bit was proposed by Firestorm in September 2012 explicitly to attract creators to OpenSim and does not stop Copybot-style theft.

checks.note: not searched (budget); consistent with prior knowledge

claims.claim: The August 2013 ToS Section 2.3 revision caused creators to fear Linden Lab could sell or license their content; the July 16, 2014 revision limited use to 'inworld or otherwise on the Service' and required an undefined 'affirmative action' for sublicensing.

checks.note: not searched (budget); consistent with prior knowledge

claims.claim: AOUSD ratified OpenUSD Core Specification 1.0 in March 2026 with a new Characters, Motion and Interactivity interest group, and on July 21, 2026 added ByteDance, Huawei, Physicl and Unity and began ISO certification of Core Spec 1.1.

checks.note: Core Spec 1.0 was released/ratified around early January 2026 (Digital Production Jan 5, 2026), not March. March 25, 2026 release announced 7 new general members and the CMI interest group (charter approved Mar 2, 2026). July 21, 2026 part confirmed: ByteDance, Huawei, Physicl, Unity as General Members; ISO process begun for Core Spec 1.1; public GitHub repo (https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/aousd-drives-global-3d-data-interoperability-ai-workflows-with-core-spec-milestones-and-members).

claims.claim: Netflix acquired Ready Player Me on December 19, 2025 and RPM shut down its public services, including the PlayerZero creator, on January 31, 2026; apps can no longer create or update avatars.

checks.note: Acquisition reported December 22, 2025, not Dec 19 (no extract supports Dec 19); price undisclosed, ~20 staff moving. Shutdown of external services Jan 31, 2026 confirmed (Schultz: creator tools Jan 30), PlayerZero and Avatar Creator SDK included.

claims.claim: VRChat's Avatar Marketplace (announced May 14, 2025; rules effective August 15, 2025) requires sellers to be 18+, sets a 600-credit minimum per distinct avatar, requires $100 earned credits for payout with one request per two weeks, and does not publish the revenue split.

checks.note: $100 minimum payout confirmed in Program Rules. Conflicts: seller FAQ floor 1,200 Credits (~$10) not 600; payout page says 30,000-credit (~$150) minimum, once per day, 1.5% fee, not one per two weeks. Revenue split is published on the welcome page: ~50% creator / ~30% store platform / ~20% VRChat+Tilia. May 14 and Aug 15, 2025 dates and 18+ rule not found (not refuted).

claims.claim: VRChat averaged about 120,000 concurrent users on weekends in 2025 with a company-cited record of 158,192 concurrents; a 2025 arXiv sample of SL users had mean ages ~45 (men, n=960) and ~38.6 (women, n=522), and no official SL age/gender breakdown after 2008 (41% female) was found.

checks.note: ~120,000 weekend concurrents by 2025 per VRChat staff (wiki: 120-125k). 158,192 is the corrected count (orig. 156,716) for the Feb 15, 2026 Kaguya concert, i.e. a 2026 record not 2025; NYE 2025-26 peak 148,886. arXiv 2505.00287 age/sample figures not searched (unverified sub-claim).

additional_findings: HB May 15, 2026: 149,536 regions, 48,376 actives public OpenSim; OSgrid 4,420 actives; registered users down ~15,000 because EdMondo stopped reporting (https://www.hypergridbusiness.com/2026/05/opensim-users-land-area-both-up-this-month/).
Jan 2026 grid ranking: Wolf Territories Grid 11,708 actives (1st), OSgrid 3,931 (2nd).
Separate HB item 'OSgrid enters immediate long-term maintenance' (https://hypergridbusiness.com/?p=78935); no source confirms OSgrid reopened after June 21, 2026.
CCUG week 33 (Aug 14, 2026): glTF 2.0 spec foundations, blend shapes, custom rigs listed; no OpenUSD mention. Week 27 hinted LL leaning back toward Vulkan; no plans to extend prims.
Project Zero Avatar Picker ported to SL Mobile; a streamed Firestorm variant was also run briefly.
AOUSD Core Spec 1.1 targets animation-spline parity with OpenUSD 25.08; July 2026 members joined at General Member level (no steering seat).
